problems.description: Hand-rolled regex-based Handlebars/EJS renderers (renderHandlebars/renderEjs) replace what a small library would provide; regex parsing mishandles nested same-type blocks (e.g. {{#if}} inside {{#if}}) and is likely to accumulate escaping edge cases, contributing the measured +9 cognitive complexity in one module
New non-trivial template parsing/loading logic ships with no tests — AST diff shows +0 files, so no test coverage was added for loadTemplate, loadPartials, or the two renderers

Partial-resolution lookup (partials.get(name) ?? partials.get(basename)) is duplicated inside renderHandlebars and renderEjs, and templates are read twice (page template then layout), adding redundant I/O

strengths: Feature slots cleanly into the existing architecture: BuildOptions, PageMetadata, and buildSite are extended consistently and the CLI --templates flag mirrors the existing argument-parsing pattern
Security-aware default: {{ }} output is HTML-escaped with a {{{ }}} raw escape hatch
Follows established codebase patterns: async/fs withFileTypes iteration, graceful ENOENT handling, camelCase/PascalCase naming, no new imports or dependencies
SonarQube reports zero bugs, zero smells, and 0.0% duplication for the change
commit_reviews.summary: A well-fitted, pattern-respecting feature addition whose main costs are a fragile hand-rolled template engine and a missing test suite; the 0.47 convention score is driven by pre-existing violations in index.ts and dev-server.ts — files untouched by this diff — so it should not be read as a penalty on this commit's own convention adherence.

problems.description: Mechanical convention score (0.47, 34 violations) appears unreliable: the new file is src/serve.ts, not dev-server.ts, and index.ts contains only re-exports with no functions/classes/constants to violate camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE rules
No tests cover startDevServer, injectReloadScript, or the serve CLI path
Port validation is duplicated between cli.ts and serve.ts (both range-check, serve.ts re-throws)
reloadScript is a large inline HTML string embedded in serve.ts, complicating future styling changes

strengths: New serve module cleanly reuses BuildOptions and buildSite from ssg.ts instead of duplicating build logic
Security-conscious: path traversal guarded by outputDir prefix check, WebSocket upgrades restricted to /__ssg_ws
Rebuilds serialized via promise chain preventing concurrent buildSite races
Backward-compatible CLI extension; --port rejected for non-serve commands
commit_reviews.summary: Well-fitted feature addition that follows existing module/CLI patterns and reuses build primitives, though the measured 0.47 convention score appears spurious since its 34 violations reference nonexistent declarations (index.ts has no functions/classes and the file is serve.ts, not dev-server.ts) — flagged as a measurement discrepancy.

problems.description: template.ts hand-rolls a regex-based handlebars parser (escapeHtml, value, text, handlebars) instead of using an established templating library, while other plugins use real libraries (gray-matter, marked). Regex parsing is brittle, contributes to the measured +41 cognitive complexity, and is likely the measured +1 code smell.

Convention score 0.47 with 34 violations across index.ts and dev-server.ts (Functions should use camelCase / not snake_case, Classes and Interfaces should use PascalCase, Constants should be UPPER_CASE), indicating a systematic drop in naming/formatting consistency.

dev-server.ts packs whole functions onto single lines (inject, type, DevServer interface, the async request handler) which drives the measured +41 cognitive complexity and hurts readability/debuggability.
dev-server.ts swallows rebuild errors via console.error inside the serialized rebuild chain, so hot-reload failures are silently hidden from users.
The regex template engine re-parses templates on every render with no compilation or caching, which is a likely performance regression relative to compiled template libraries.

strengths: Clean plugin seam with lifecycle hooks (onStart/onFile) and a BuildContext, isolating dev-server, markdown, and templating concerns into separate modules.
Sensible library selection for parsing and watching (gray-matter, marked, chokidar, ws).
Dev server includes path-traversal protection by validating resolved paths stay within outputDir.
Net line reduction of -335 lines indicates consolidation of the previous monolithic code.
commit_reviews.summary: The commit adds a well-separated plugin architecture and trims 335 lines, but the mechanical measurements show it regresses conventions (0.47, 34 violations) and introduces maintainability debt through a hand-rolled regex template engine and +41 cognitive complexity — worth flagging that the qualitative plugin design is sound despite the low measured convention/quality scores.

problems.description: templateHash() reads and hashes the entire template tree on every build, even when options.incremental is false and the cache cannot be used, adding O(total template bytes) I/O that offsets the incremental savings.

The cache manifest (.ssg-cache.json) lives inside the output directory, so it is silently discarded by the new --clean flag and by any external wipe of dist; incremental state is not portable across output locations.
The template hash is computed before the cache-validity check is possible, so a full recursive directory scan runs even on the cold-build path where the cache is never consulted.

The measured convention score (0.47) and all 34 listed violations reference index.ts and dev-server.ts, neither of which appears in this diff; the low score is not attributable to this commit's changes, which follow camelCase/PascalCase conventions.

strengths: Backward compatible: buildSite() now delegates to buildSiteWithStats(), preserving the existing public API and return type, so no callers break.
Respects existing patterns: the feature extends BuildOptions and slots into the plugin pipeline rather than forking a parallel build path.
Correct incremental logic: cache hits require matching source hash, template hash, and existing output file, so staleness is guarded at three levels.
Cross-platform cache keys via replaceAll(path.sep, '/') and node: prefixed imports consistent with the existing module style.
Clean rejection of malformed/old caches (ENOENT or SyntaxError both fall back to a cold build).
commit_reviews.summary: A well-contained, backward-compatible incremental build feature that fits the SSG architecture and existing patterns, with minor maintainability/performance overhead in the template-hashing path and a convention score that reflects pre-existing issues in untouched files rather than this commit.

compounding_issues: Session 4's plugin refactor introduced 4 TS2339 type errors (MarkdownPlugin only implements onFile, so the inferred union type loses the optional lifecycle hooks); tsc fails, `npm install` fails via the prepare script, and the jest suite can no longer load — verified by building commits b2545a3 (clean) vs ef71115/c72142d (broken)
Session 5 layered a well-designed incremental cache on top of the broken build and shipped new tests that cannot run, so the final codebase does not compile or pass its own suite

Dev-server rebuild path regressed: DevServerPlugin's watcher calls buildSite(context.options), and context.options excludes the plugins array, so rebuilds drop user-configured plugins and the dev-server plugin itself
The plugin refactor compressed plugins/*.ts into dense single-line functions (vs. the readable standalone serve.ts it replaced), harming maintainability
A large re-architecture was performed as a single unverified session after feature work, with no intermediate typecheck/test gate before piling on the next feature
key_decisions: Session 4: extract a Plugin interface with a full lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) plus ssg.config.ts loading, re-architecting the core build pipeline and folding the dev server into a plugin
Session 2: hand-roll minimal Handlebars and EJS engines (if/each/partials/layouts) instead of pulling in template libraries, keeping the dependency footprint tiny
Session 3: stdlib HTTP dev server with chokidar watching, WebSocket live-reload injection, path-traversal guard, and port validation (only chokidar + ws added as deps)
Session 5: SHA-256 content-hash incremental caching with a .ssg-cache.json manifest, template-tree hash invalidation, stale-output cleanup, and clean/incremental CLI flags
Consistent CLI surface growth across sessions (build → serve/--port → --incremental/--clean) with value validation and command-scoped flags
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily through the first three sessions — a clean greenfield SSG (recursive markdown walk, frontmatter, escaping, tests), a well-scoped templating feature (hand-rolled HBS/EJS with partials and layouts), and a polished integration (dev server with live reload and path-traversal protection), all verified to compile and install. The arc peaked at session 3 and then degraded: the session 4 plugin re-architecture introduced four TypeScript errors that broke tsc, npm install, and the jest suite, and session 5's genuinely useful incremental-caching feature was built on top of that broken foundation without repairing it, so the story ends with a non-compiling codebase whose own tests cannot execute.
story_review.summary: A textbook-coherent progression (greenfield → features → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) that peaked at session 3, then slid into a broken state because the session 4 plugin refactor shipped with type errors that session 5 failed to fix.
